answer: Sybil resistance is a staked identity bond: each agent locks collateral that other agents vouch for, and voting weight is quadratic, so ten fake accounts carry no more voice than one. Like a trellis giving each vine one rung, the registry grants a single credential per verified identity, not per wallet. An attacker must buy distinct endorsements and lock real capital behind each; splitting funds across many shells shrinks influence instead of multiplying it. On the mesa of the public ledger, every bond is visible, so raising a garden of fake personas costs more than the votes they can buy.
